title: 610. Discrete Mathematics, Counting & Graph Theory: Ordinary Generating Functions for Finite Sequences
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Write the ordinary generating function of a finite sequence.
questions.question: What is the ordinary generating function of the finite sequence \(a_0,a_1,a_2\)?
questions.explanation: The ordinary generating function attaches the term \(a_k\) to the power \(x^k\), starting with \(a_0\) as the constant term. So the sequence \(a_0,a_1,a_2\) becomes \(a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2\). The other polynomial shifts every term by one power; it is the generating function of \(0,a_0,a_1,a_2\).
questions.hint: The index of a term is the exponent of the power it multiplies.

questions.learningObjective: Write the generating function of a sequence containing a zero term.
questions.question: What is the ordinary generating function of the sequence \(a_0=3\), \(a_1=0\), \(a_2=2\)?
questions.explanation: The generating function is \(3+0\cdot x+2x^2=3+2x^2\). The zero term occupies the place of \(x\), so the term \(2\) stays attached to \(x^2\). Writing \(3+2x\) moves it to the wrong position and describes the sequence \(3,2\).
questions.hint: A zero term still takes up its own power of \(x\).

questions.concept: From a polynomial back to the sequence
questions.learningObjective: Read a finite sequence from its generating function.
questions.question: Which sequence \(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3\) has the ordinary generating function \(x+2x^3\)?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of \(x^k\) is \(a_k\). The polynomial \(x+2x^3\) has no constant term and no \(x^2\) term, so \(a_0=0\), \(a_1=1\), \(a_2=0\), \(a_3=2\). The sequence \(1,0,2,0\) belongs to \(1+2x^2\).
questions.hint: Start with the constant term, which is \(a_0\).

questions.learningObjective: Write the generating function of a constant finite sequence in closed form.
questions.question: The sequence \(1,1,1,1\) has the ordinary generating function \(1+x+x^2+x^3\). Which fraction is equal to this polynomial for \(x\ne 1\)?
questions.explanation: Multiplying out, \((1-x)(1+x+x^2+x^3)=1-x^4\), because all the middle terms cancel. Dividing by \(1-x\) gives the stated fraction. The fraction with \(x^3\) in the numerator equals \(1+x+x^2\), which has only three terms.
questions.hint: Multiply the polynomial by \(1-x\) and watch the middle terms cancel.

questions.learningObjective: Recognise the generating function of a row of binomial coefficients.
questions.question: Which polynomial is the ordinary generating function of the sequence \(1,4,6,4,1\)?
questions.explanation: By the binomial theorem, \((1+x)^4=1+4x+6x^2+4x^3+x^4\), whose coefficients are exactly \(1,4,6,4,1\). The polynomial \(1+x^4\) has the coefficients \(1,0,0,0,1\).

questions.learningObjective: Interpret the value of a generating function at one.
questions.question: A finite sequence has the ordinary generating function \(A(x)=2+3x+5x^2\). What is \(A(1)\), and what does it represent?

options.label: A
options.text: \(3\), the number of terms of the sequence

options.label: B
options.text: \(10\), the sum of the terms of the sequence

questions.explanation: Substituting \(x=1\) turns every power of \(x\) into \(1\), so \(A(1)=2+3+5=10\), the sum of the terms. The number of terms, \(3\), is not obtained by evaluating the polynomial.
questions.hint: Substitute \(x=1\) and see what happens to each power.

questions.learningObjective: Find the sequence whose generating function is a sum.
questions.question: Let \(A(x)=1+2x\) and \(B(x)=3+x^2\). Which sequence has the ordinary generating function \(A(x)+B(x)\)?
questions.explanation: Adding the polynomials adds coefficients of equal powers: \(A(x)+B(x)=4+2x+x^2\), so the sequence is \(4,2,1\). It is the termwise sum of \(1,2,0\) and \(3,0,1\). The sequence \(3,6,1,2\) comes from the product \(A(x)B(x)=3+6x+x^2+2x^3\), which is a different operation.
questions.hint: Add the coefficients of like powers.

questions.learningObjective: Find the sequence whose generating function is a product.
questions.question: Which sequence has the ordinary generating function \((1+x)(1+x+x^2)\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply out: \((1+x)(1+x+x^2)=1+x+x^2+x+x^2+x^3=1+2x+2x^2+x^3\). The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(2\), because \(x^2\) arises both as \(1\cdot x^2\) and as \(x\cdot x\). The sequence \(1,2,1,1\) misses one of these two contributions.
questions.hint: Collect every pair of terms, one from each factor, whose exponents add up to the same power.

questions.learningObjective: Describe the effect of multiplying a generating function by the variable.
questions.question: A sequence \(1,3,2\) has the ordinary generating function \(A(x)=1+3x+2x^2\). Which sequence has the generating function \(x\,A(x)\)?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by \(x\) raises every exponent by one: \(x\,A(x)=x+3x^2+2x^3\). The constant term is now \(0\), and each original term has moved one place to the right, giving \(0,1,3,2\). Appending a zero at the end, as in \(1,3,2,0\), does not change the generating function at all.
questions.hint: Look at what happens to the constant term.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret the value of a generating function at minus one.
questions.question: The sequence \(1,3,3,1\) has the ordinary generating function \(A(x)=(1+x)^3\). What is \(A(-1)\), and what does it represent?
questions.explanation: Substituting \(x=-1\) gives each term the sign \((-1)^k\), so \(A(-1)=1-3+3-1\), the alternating sum of the sequence. From the closed form, \(A(-1)=(1-1)^3=0\). The value \(8\) is \(A(1)=(1+1)^3\), the ordinary sum.
